query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a titanium diboride (TiB2) coating on boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment will improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion by forming a stable, protective interfacial layer that resists chemical attack and minimizes diffusion of aluminum into the substrate.
generation.material_initial_state: Boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, without any additional protective coatings.
generation.intervention: Application of a titanium diboride (TiB2) coating to the surface of the boride-based components.
generation.conditions: Molten aluminum environment at typical operating temperatures for hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment (e.g., 660–750°C).
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable TiB2 interfacial layer that resists chemical interaction with molten aluminum.
generation.mechanism: TiB2 has high chemical stability and a low solubility in molten aluminum, which prevents the formation of detrimental intermetallic compounds and reduces aluminum diffusion into the substrate, thereby enhancing corrosion resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: The TiB2-coated components will exhibit significantly reduced corrosion rates compared to uncoated boride-based components, with an improvement of at least 50% in corrosion resistance under the specified conditions.
generation.baseline: Corrosion resistance of uncoated boride-based components in molten aluminum under identical conditions.
generation.boundary: The improvement is expected to hold as long as the operating temperature does not exceed the thermal stability limit of TiB2 and the coating remains intact without significant mechanical damage.
generation.uncertainty: The extent of improvement in corrosion resistance depends on the quality and uniformity of the TiB2 coating, as well as the specific composition of the boride substrate and molten aluminum alloy.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of boride-based components: one with a TiB2 coating and one without. Expose both sets to molten aluminum at 700°C for a fixed duration (e.g., 100 hours). Measure the mass loss and analyze the surface morphology and composition using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS).
measurements: Chemical composition of the surface and interfacial layers
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the TiB2-coated components do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in mass loss or show similar levels of corrosion and intermetallic formation as the uncoated components, the hypothesis will be falsified.
